title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying a group (scheme) M_{ρ,σ} attached to two elements ρ, σ, each satisfying a quadratic Hamilton–Cayley equation (for σ: σ^2 − v = 0). It is built from a torus T_0, the 'quadratic' tori T_ρ and T_σ (units of the rank-2 algebras generated by ρ and σ), a normalizer N'_σ, and a group G (or SG). There is a homomorphism Θ: M_{ρ,σ} → G. On the previous page he shows that the kernel SR°_{ρ,σ} of Θ° is isomorphic to ST_ρ × ST_σ, the product of the norm-one subtori. He also shows M_{ρ,σ}/SR° ≅ G × μ2 × μ2, via (Θ, ε1, ε2), and that G acts trivially on SR° by conjugation.

On this page:
(i) He determines how the quotient μ2 × μ2 acts on SR° ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ. He uses the subgroup M_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, which surjects onto μ2 × μ2 via (ε3, ε2).
(ii) Result: only the second factor acts, where ε2(u,a,b) = ε_σ(b). An element ε (ε^2 = 1) fixes ST_ρ and acts on T_σ, hence on ST_σ, by σ ↦ εσ (68). This is compatible with σ^2 − v = 0. For ε = −1 it is the Galois conjugation of the quadratic algebra O[σ]/(σ^2 − v), i.e. the inversion/conjugation on the norm-one torus. A crossed-out passage abandons an attempt to locate G_m ⊂ G inside M_{ρ,σ}(0).
(iii) Step 5°: R°_{ρ,σ} is defined as Θ^{-1}(G_m), the preimage of the scalar subgroup (centre) of G inside M°_{ρ,σ}. This gives the central-type extension (70): 1 → SR° → R° → G_m → 1.
(iv) Explicitly, R° consists of the elements (u,a,b)·f with u ∈ T_0, a ∈ T_ρ, b ∈ T_σ and f ∈ SG, such that det u = det a = det b and u f is scalar. Equivalently f = λ u^{-1} with λ ∈ G_m and λ^2 = det u.

The next page parametrizes R° by μ (via the map j), shows R° → T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ is the pull-back of squaring μ ↦ μ^2 on G_m, and proves R° = Centre(M°).

Purpose: a structural analysis (kernel, centre, component group, outer action) of the group M_{ρ,σ}. This group arises in Grothendieck's study of solutions of the 'loop equation' in rank 2, i.e. linear-algebraic data with prescribed quadratic local monodromies, presumably related to the Teichmüller tower / modular-group relations. A marginal note flags the interest of R_{ρ,σ} for a later 'realization (102)' of M_{ρ,σ} and refers to step (6°).
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The step 'f = λu^{-1} with λ^2 = det u' presupposes det f = 1 (f ∈ SG), which is consistent with the subscript ΓSG under f in the image.
The scope of the claim that μ2 × μ2 acts 'via its second factor' depends on definitions given on earlier pages (ε3, M_{ρ,σ}(0)), which cannot be checked from this page.

ideas.what: Kernel SR° ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ (product of norm-one tori of quadratic algebras), with the component group μ2×μ2 acting through Galois conjugation σ ↦ −σ on one factor
ideas.modern_name: Norm-one torus of a quadratic étale algebra; outer action of the component group of a normalizer of a torus
ideas.where_published: General torus theory is in SGA 3; this specific computation is unpublished

ideas.what: R° = preimage of the scalar G_m under Θ, giving an extension of G_m by ST_ρ×ST_σ, later identified with the centre of M° and with a squaring pull-back of T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ
ideas.modern_name: Centre of a disconnected reductive group scheme; fibre product of tori over the determinant

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine structural computation of the centre, kernel and outer action for an auxiliary group scheme in the loop-equation notes. It is technically correct but contains no new idea beyond standard torus theory.
transcription_corrections: The symbol under SR° is a rotated ≃ (isomorphism SR° ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ), not '\wr\shortparallel'.
Under f the image shows f ∈ ΓSG (not ΓG); under b it shows ΓT_σ.
The marginal note reads approximately: 'N.B. voir : intérêt de [?] ... sur l'intérêt de R_{ρ,σ} et la réalisation (102) plus bas de M_{ρ,σ} ... cf. (6°)'.
The final line reads 'i.e. f = λu^{-1} où λ ∈ ΓG_m, λ^2 = det u'.
The archive page number '423' is written at the bottom left; the author's page number (513/514) is not on this sheet.
